old_description: If you have any questions about anything in the store or about your order
about:
Tools for Working Wood operates a retail showroom and online store in Brooklyn, New York. The business has been active since at least 1999, as indicated by its website copyright. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed, though a blog authored by someone named Joel appears on the site, suggesting a founder or key figure.

The company sells a curated selection of woodworking tools and accessories, including draw knives, bow saw kits, and hardware kits for handle attachment. It maintains a physical showroom open weekdays from 9:00 to 5:00 and provides telephone customer service during business hours. Orders can be shipped internationally, and the site includes a guarantee and return policy.

The primary customers are woodworkers, carpenters, and craft enthusiasts seeking hand tools and specialty items. Products such as the Gramercy Tools Bow Saw Kits and spoonmaker’s draw knives illustrate the focus on traditional hand-tool woodworking. The store also offers hardware kits for attaching handles to draw knives.

The company emphasizes a personal investment in craft, offering a guarantee and return policy alongside direct phone support. Its Brooklyn location allows local customers to visit the showroom, while the online store serves a broader audience. The site is coded in New York and powered by a local technology partner.

name: Tosoh SMD, Inc.
old_description: High purity metals and alloys for the Semiconductor Industry.
about:
Tosoh SMD, Inc. operates from a facility on Gantz Road in Grove City, Ohio. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure in public materials, though it operates under the Tosoh corporate umbrella as suggested by the "Tosoh Global" branding and copyright notices.

The company manufactures consumable materials for thin-film deposition, including sputtering targets for semiconductor, flat-panel display, and solar applications. Its product lines cover high-purity aluminum, copper, tantalum, and titanium targets, as well as gas-atomized metal powders specialized for difficult high-purity alloys. Tosoh SMD also produces a portfolio of proprietary chemical precursors—such as RuDER® for ruthenium and ruthenium oxide, Rudense® for area-selective deposition, and a series of Ts- and Si-based precursors—for advanced semiconductor processes.

These materials serve customers in the semiconductor, flat-panel display, solar photovoltaic, and organic light-emitting diode (OLED) industries. The company positions itself as a supplier to manufacturers requiring high-purity consumables for deposition processes, though specific customer names are not disclosed.

Tosoh SMD’s stated mission is to be the preferred global supplier of high-technology consumable materials for thin-film deposition, emphasizing technological and commercial excellence, on-time delivery, supply-chain quality, and continuous improvement.

name: TouchPad Electronics LLC
old_description: Sub-assembly services as well as design and manufacturing of touchscreen and digital displays, UI, cable and harnesses, and test fixtures.
about:
TouchPad Electronics LLC is based in Mukwonago, Wisconsin. The company was founded in 2000 as TouchPad Design Corporation, a privately owned electrical engineering and PCB layout design firm that offered ultra-fast turnaround for advanced technology PCB designs. This early focus forged a culture of urgency, quality, and responsiveness that continues today.

Today TouchPad provides end-to-end electronics manufacturing services, including PCB design and layout, quick-turn prototype and production assembly, microcontroller-based design, flexible circuit and membrane switch design, and RF, analog, and digital circuit engineering. The company also handles sub-assembly, touchscreen and digital display manufacturing, user interface design, cable and harness assembly, and test fixture fabrication. Operations are housed in a 22,500‑square‑foot facility equipped with six SMT and selective soldering lines, automated optical inspection, X‑ray inspection, and multiple flex placement machines. Staffing has grown significantly since 2010, with the engineering and technical team expanding through multiple hiring phases.

TouchPad serves customers in medical, industrial, consumer, and advanced research sectors, including organizations involved in industrial control and human‑machine interface (HMI) technology. The company describes its client base as the “who’s who” in those markets, emphasizing relationships where quality, delivery, and value are prime factors.

The company’s stated mission is to provide unmatched technical value by applying superior processes with a sense of urgency and innovation to deliver timely results and product excellence. TouchPad differentiates itself with a custom ERP system that enables live component sourcing—reportedly establishing 95 % of component availability and pricing within minutes—and a quoting turnaround of less than 24 hours. ISO 9001:2008 registration covers hardware, software, mechanical engineering, PCB layout, and manufacturing.

name: Tower Manufacturing Corporation
old_description: Tower Manufacturing is a Leading  Manufacturer of Electrical Safety Devices and Electromechanical Products.
about:
Tower Manufacturing Corporation was founded in 1957 by Louis Shatkin in Providence, Rhode Island. The company remains under his active leadership and has grown from a regional operation into an international supplier with manufacturing sites in Providence and Shenzhen, China, plus sales offices in Hong Kong and Taiwan.

The company produces electrical safety devices — including ground-fault circuit interrupters (GFCI), leakage-current detection interrupters (LCDI), equipment leakage-current interrupters (ELCI), and appliance leakage-current interrupters (ALCI) — as well as electromechanical components such as printed circuit board assemblies, thermostats, switches, windings, solenoids, wire harnesses, and overload protection. Its Shenzhen facility spans roughly 250,000 square feet and employs about 3,000 production workers, while the Providence headquarters houses an engineering team with over 100 years of combined design experience and an on-site laboratory where qualification testing is witnessed by UL and cUL representatives.

Tower serves the construction, commercial/industrial, and residential markets, and provides OEM safety products to Fortune 500 companies. The firm participates in standards bodies including NEMA, NFPA, AHAM, and NEC, and sits on UL’s 1699 STP committee for LCDI/AFCI.

The business was built on Shatkin’s pioneering work in GFCI technology, which has yielded more than 20 patents. Tower emphasizes safety-first design to UL and CSA standards, rapid custom development, and a vertically integrated model that keeps qualification testing in-house under UL supervision.

Toyotetsu America, Inc. (TTAI) operates from Somerset, Kentucky, as part of Toyotetsu North America, a network that includes facilities in Owensboro, Kentucky; San Antonio, Texas; Simcoe, Ontario; and Guanajuato, Mexico. The company traces its roots back more than 25 years, establishing itself as a supplier of stamped and welded body components for the automotive sector.

TTAI specializes in metal stamping, welding, and assembly of body parts and structural assemblies for automotive manufacturers. Its production footprint spans multiple plants across North America, each equipped for high-volume stamping and robotic welding lines, though specific facility sizes and annual output figures are not publicly disclosed.

The company serves the automotive industry, providing components to original equipment manufacturers. Its customer base includes major automakers, though specific client names are not listed in the available information.

TTAI emphasizes lean manufacturing principles and operates state-of-the-art training centers at its locations to develop workforce skills. The company highlights its long tenure, employee-focused benefits, and job stability as factors that support consistent production quality.

name: Transpacific Food Inc
old_description: From berries to fruit to high-quality purees, Transpacific Food brings you nature’s best.
about:
Transpacific Food Inc opened its doors in 2000 in Salem, Oregon, under the leadership of CEO Bob Underwood, a third-generation farmer whose family experience in agriculture shapes the company’s approach. The business began with a focus on delivering high-quality fruit products to buyers seeking reliable sourcing and consistent quality.

The company produces high-quality fruit purees and creates custom formulations tailored to client specifications for color, consistency, and flavor. Its laboratory serves as an R&D partner, developing pure fruit blends for both large manufacturers needing agility and smaller brands requiring cost-effective product development. Transpacific sources berries and fruit from domestic and international growers, managing a supply chain that includes rigorous quality assurance, food safety documentation, and hands-on inspections at grower and co-packer facilities. The operation handles orders ranging from unique small batches to million-pound volumes, and also assists with logistics, packaging, and labeling challenges.

Transpacific serves fruit buyers across the food and beverage industry, including ingredient suppliers, processors, and brands developing new products. Larger companies leverage the firm’s formulation expertise and flexible production, while smaller businesses use its R&D services to bring products to market. The company’s customer base spans any sector requiring consistent, high-quality fruit ingredients.

The company says its differentiation lies in a vast sourcing network that draws from the Pacific Northwest and global regions, combined with a stringent approval process that includes in-person inspections of every grower and co-packer. Its mission emphasizes innovation, creativity, integrity, and efficiency, aiming to be the first call for fruit buyers. The leadership’s generational farming background informs a commitment to delivering fruit at peak quality, backed by a quality assurance program that spans from field to delivery.

name: Treehouse Woodworking
old_description: Welcome to Treehouse Woodworking with Master Craftsman Brent Corson
about:
Treehouse Woodworking operates from Concord, New Hampshire, where it was founded in 2008 by master craftsman Brent Corson. The shop began as a custom design and build operation focused on residential and commercial woodworking projects.

The company produces a range of custom woodwork including stair systems, kitchen cabinetry, built-in furniture, architectural mouldings, mantels, library systems, home theater cabinetry, and pet furniture. All pieces are designed and fabricated in-house, with capabilities spanning from initial design through final installation for both new construction and renovation projects.

Treehouse serves homeowners, architects, builders, and interior designers across residential and commercial sectors. Projects have included custom stairways for private residences, built-in cabinetry for commercial offices, and specialized pet furniture for retail clients.

The firm emphasizes its over 20 years of custom design and building experience, with Corson’s master craftsman designation underscoring a commitment to traditional joinery and tailored solutions rather than mass-produced alternatives.
